column2: The mercurial director could be charming at breakfast and furious by noon, leaving the crew guessing.
column3: 這位導演性情多變，早餐時風度翩翩，中午就怒氣沖沖，讓劇組團隊摸不著頭緒。
column5: 水星 Mercury 的水銀滑來滑去抓不住，像情緒善變的人

column2: Oil prices remained volatile throughout the crisis, rising and falling sharply from one week to the next.
column3: 危機期間油價一直動盪不安，每週都大起大落。
column5: 酒精一打開就揮發飛走，局勢也像這樣一碰就變

column2: His erratic attendance, present for a week and then absent for months, made the course impossible to plan.
column3: 他出席時有時無，來一週又缺席數月，使課程無法規劃。
column5: err 是犯錯，路線走錯又亂繞，行蹤飄忽不定

column2: She vacillated between taking the job abroad and staying near her family until the deadline passed.
column3: 她在出國工作與留在家人身邊之間猶豫不決，直到期限已過。
column4: vacillate between options (在選項間猶豫)
column5: 想像天秤晃來晃去，拿不定主意

column2: Her confidence wavered when the judges began asking sharper questions.
column3: 評審開始提出更尖銳的問題時，她的信心動搖了。
column5: wave 揮動，旗子隨風揮來揮去，決心也晃動

column2: Public opinion oscillated between hope and despair as the negotiations dragged on.
column3: 隨著談判一再拖延，民意在希望與絕望之間來回擺盪。
column4: oscillate between extremes (在兩極間擺盪)
column5: 想像電風扇搖頭，左右來回擺盪

column2: Irresolute leaders, afraid of offending anyone, let the crisis deepen while they debated.
column3: 優柔寡斷的領導者怕得罪任何人，一邊爭論，一邊任由危機惡化。
column4: irresolute leader (優柔寡斷的領導者)
column5: ir 不 + resolute 堅決 = 不堅決，拿不定主意

column2: Managing three research projects at once proved taxing, even for such an experienced scientist.
column3: 同時負責三項研究計畫相當吃力，即使是這麼有經驗的科學家也一樣。
column5: tax 稅金壓得人喘不過氣，taxing 就是壓力很重

column2: The arduous climb to the summit took eleven hours in thin air.
column3: 攀上山頂的艱苦路程，在稀薄的空氣中花了十一小時。
column5: 想像爬陡坡累得喘「啊嘟斯」，艱苦費力

column2: Her exacting standards meant every draft came back with dozens of corrections.
column3: 她的標準嚴格，每份草稿都被退回並附上數十處修改。
column5: exact 精確，要求精確到分毫，所以苛求

column2: Years of painstaking restoration returned the fresco to something close to its original brilliance.
column3: 多年煞費苦心的修復，讓這幅壁畫幾乎重現當初的光彩。
column5: pains 辛苦 + taking 花費 = 花盡苦心

column2: The punctilious clerk checked every signature, date, and stamp before approving the form.
column3: 這位一絲不苟的職員，核准表格前逐一檢查每個簽名、日期和印章。
column5: punct 是「點」，連一個小點都要計較

column2: A scrupulous editor, she verified every quotation against its original source.
column3: 她是個嚴謹的編輯，每句引文都對照原始出處查證。
column5: scruple 是良心的顧慮，凡事怕過不了良心這關

column2: After the fever broke, he was lucid enough to recall the conversation clearly.
column3: 退燒之後，他神智清醒，能清楚回想起那場談話。
column5: luc 是光，像開了燈，腦袋或文字都亮晶晶

column2: The lawyer's perspicuous summary let jurors grasp the complex contract in minutes.
column3: 律師表達清楚的摘要，讓陪審員幾分鐘內就看懂複雜的合約。
column5: per 穿過 + spic 看，一眼就看穿，清楚易懂

column2: The origin of the custom is obscure, since no written records survive.
column3: 這項習俗的起源不明，因為沒有留下任何文字紀錄。
column5: 想像起霧的窗戶，後面的東西看不清楚

column2: The opaque wording of the contract concealed what the fees really were.
column3: 合約晦澀難解的措辭，掩蓋了費用的真相。
column5: 反義是 transparent 透明；opaque 像毛玻璃看不透

column2: Few readers could follow the abstruse argument, which relied on obscure mathematical notation.
column3: 很少讀者能跟上這套深奧的論證，它依賴冷僻的數學符號。
column5: abs 離開 + trus 推，被推到遠處的深奧道理

column2: The professor's recondite footnotes cited manuscripts that only a handful of scholars had ever seen.
column3: 教授深奧冷僻的註腳，引用了只有少數學者見過的手稿。
column5: re 回 + condite 藏，藏在深處很少人知道

column2: The club's esoteric rituals meant nothing to outsiders but were precious to its members.
column3: 這個社團的秘傳儀式，對外人毫無意義，對成員卻很珍貴。
column4: esoteric language (圈內人才懂的語言)
column5: eso 是「內」，只有內圈的人才懂

column2: Tax law is full of arcane rules that baffle even trained accountants.
column3: 稅法充滿難解的神祕規定，連受過訓練的會計師也一頭霧水。
column5: arca 是古老的箱子，裡面鎖著祕密

column2: The Mona Lisa's enigmatic smile has puzzled viewers for centuries.
column3: 蒙娜麗莎如謎般的微笑，數百年來一直讓觀眾困惑。
column5: enigma 是謎，enigmatic 就是像謎一樣

column2: The inscrutable expression on the negotiator's face gave away nothing about his intentions.
column3: 談判代表高深莫測的表情，完全沒透露他的意圖。
column5: in 不 + scrut 查看，無法看透

column2: A sincere apology helped mollify the customer, who had been waiting two hours.
column3: 誠懇的道歉安撫了那位已經等了兩小時的顧客。
column4: mollify an angry client (安撫憤怒的客戶)
column5: moll 是軟，讓硬邦邦的怒氣變軟

column2: The mayor tried to placate protesters by promising a public hearing.
column3: 市長承諾舉辦公開聽證會，試圖平息抗議民眾的怒氣。
column5: plac 是平靜，像 placid 平靜的湖面

column2: Critics say that trying to appease an aggressor by conceding territory only encourages further demands.
column3: 批評者說，讓出領土來安撫侵略者，只會招來更多要求。
column5: ap + peace 和平，用讓步換取暫時和平

column2: A cup of warm tea did little to assuage her fear before the exam.
column3: 一杯熱茶對緩和她考前的恐懼沒什麼幫助。
column5: 裡面有 sweet 的音，甜甜的東西讓痛苦減輕

column2: The envoy sought to conciliate the rival factions with small concessions on both sides.
column3: 使節試圖讓雙方各退一步，來調解敵對的派系。
column4: conciliate rival groups (調解敵對團體)
column5: council 是協商會議，conciliate 就是坐下來協商

column2: Ancient farmers offered grain to propitiate gods they believed controlled the rains.
column3: 古代農夫獻上穀物，討好他們相信掌管雨水的神明。
column5: 想像獻上供品，請神明消氣降福

column2: Skipping meals will only exacerbate your stomach pain.
column3: 不吃飯只會讓你的胃痛更嚴重。
column5: ex 加上 + acerb 酸苦，讓痛苦變得更酸

column2: Scratching the rash will only aggravate it and delay healing.
column3: 抓皮疹只會讓情況加重，也延後痊癒。
column5: ag 加上 + grav 重，像 gravity 重力，讓事情更重

column2: The evanescent glow of the sunset faded before we could photograph it.
column3: 日落的餘暉轉瞬消散，我們來不及拍下。
column5: e 出 + vanish 消失，慢慢淡出消失

column2: She caught only a fleeting glimpse of the fox before it vanished into the brush.
column3: 她只匆匆瞥見那隻狐狸，牠就消失在灌木叢裡。
column5: flee 逃跑，一溜煙就跑掉的短暫畫面

column2: Housing shortages are a perennial problem in the city, resurfacing in every election.
column3: 住房短缺是這座城市長期存在的問題，每次選舉都會再度浮現。
column5: per 貫穿 + enn 年，年年都在

column2: Scientists once believed the laws of nature were immutable, fixed for all time.
column3: 科學家曾相信自然法則是永恆不變的，永遠固定。
column5: im 不 + mut 變，像 mutant 突變的反義

column2: The novel's enduring popularity shows that readers still find its themes relevant.
column3: 這本小說歷久不衰的人氣顯示，讀者仍覺得它的主題貼近現實。
column5: endure 是忍耐撐住，經得起時間考驗的就是持久

column2: Keep your answer succinct, since the interviewer has only ten minutes.
column3: 回答要簡練，因為面試官只有十分鐘。
column5: 像把腰帶束緊 cinch，話也縮短成精華

column2: A concise report of two pages is better than a rambling one of twenty.
column3: 兩頁簡潔的報告勝過二十頁漫無邊際的報告。
column5: cis 是剪，像 scissors 把多餘的剪掉

column2: His verbose reply took three paragraphs to say what could have been said in a sentence.
column3: 他囉嗦的回覆用了三段，其實一句話就能說完。
column5: verb 是字詞，字多到滿出來

column2: The prolix author padded every chapter with lengthy digressions nobody had requested.
column3: 這位文字冗贅的作者，每一章都塞滿沒人要求的長篇岔題。
column5: 字句像水龍頭一直流個不停，停不下來
